study type: Descriptive cohort study with a comparison group
exposure: Creatine Transporter Deficiency (CTD) due to a pathogenic SLC6A8 variant
outcome: Clinical characteristics (epilepsy, behavioral disorder, axial hypotonia, ataxia, fine motor skills, language impairment, slender build, nursing care needs)
Developmental trajectory (fine/gross motor skills, language, communication/sociability)
Caregiver burden (risk of burnout, time dependence)
cohort: The study included 31 patients (27 male, 4 female) with Creatine Transporter Deficiency (CTD) defined by a pathogenic SLC6A8 variant and ID and/or autism spectrum disorder, along with an age- and sex-matched control group of patients with Fragile X syndrome.
finding: Patients with CTD exhibit consistently delayed developmental trajectories across multiple domains, a high prevalence of epilepsy and early-onset behavioral disorders, and impose a significant burden on caregivers, highlighting specific assessment tools (Vineland, PPVT5, CBI) as relevant endpoints for future therapeutic trials.
